pure-announcement.rationale: It is vendor documentation of an ongoing technique (prompt-prefix caching), not a launch, release or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest concepts (proxy capture, SIEM gaps, MCP statelessness) cover prompt caching or inference cost reduction.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The single captured claim is backed by a primary vendor docs URL any reader can check.

durability.rationale: The underlying prefix-caching mechanism ages well, but everything actually captured — the `cache_control` parameter name and the 5-minute/1-hour TTL values — is vendor feature-matrix detail that can change under the reader.

actionability.rationale: The one-sentence capture names a product knob to turn but carries none of the trade-offs (minimum cacheable lengths, pricing multipliers, invalidation rules) a builder would need to actually decide anything.

atomicity.rationale: What little was captured is exactly one idea — cache prompt prefixes at explicit breakpoints — statable in a single sentence.
